mechanism_narrative: Persistent workplace mobility decline over four weeks signals sustained remote work adoption, reducing commuter retail spending and lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -32.4% to -29.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -25% of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility falling below -32% for two consecutive weeks triggers consumer avoidance of public transit-dependent retail destinations, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -32% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -31.4% in t-0w, -31.7% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 percentage points in the two weeks following sustained TRANSIT decline below -32%.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility stability near -4% combined with residential elevation at +7.6% indicates holiday preparation behavior; this dual signal predicts RETAIL_REC recovery of at least 5 percentage points over the next four weeks as seasonal shopping accelerates.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at -3.9%, RESIDENTIAL stable at +7.6%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both show stability within ±1 percentage point.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility turning negative (from +1.9% to -1.7% over two weeks) signals outdoor activity substitution collapse, redirecting leisure spending to indoor retail venues and raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following PARKS turning negative, or PARKS rebounds above zero within the same week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls more than 2 percentage points week-on-week while WORKPLACES remains depressed below -29%, policy-driven mobility restrictions are tightening; this dual constraint suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week decline exceeds 2 points AND WORKPLACES below -29%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point over the next 14 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES constraints are simultaneously active.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility holding steady at +7.6% while RETAIL_REC declines to -21.1% indicates consumers are substituting home-based activities for in-person retail; this behavioral lock-in persists over the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +7.4% to +8.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 4 percentage points over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +7%.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility declining from -3.3% to -3.9% week-on-week signals reduced essential-trip frequency; this contraction in baseline mobility flows predicts RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed or decline further over the next week as overall consumer mobility contracts.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines more than 0.5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -3.3% to -3.9% between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM decline.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of TRANSIT collapse below -31% and PARKS turning negative signals a regime shift toward indoor-only activity; this dual constraint interaction predicts RETAIL_REC will recover as consumers shift from outdoor to indoor retail venues over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -31% AND PARKS negative simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and PARKS constraints are simultaneously active.
